cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Hand It Over
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to give up control of a task, object, or decision you believe is being mishandled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Let me handle the seating plan. You've put the exes together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then they can be civil from separate tables.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the pencil. I'll preserve the hours and move the chairs.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 decides and A3 restricts questions, but A5 pencil demand does not clearly make an approval concession to B investment.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 civility claim causes A3 separate-tables retort; B4 hours causes A5 preserve-hours metaphor, whose practical preservation is vague.

relationship.evidence: B2 defends a judgment and B4 values work already done, providing credible reasons not to hand over control.

heightening.evidence: B4 time investment causes A5 a claimed preservation promise, but the ending does not specify what work will remain.

specificity.evidence: A1 seating plan and exes together establish the perceived mishandling and desired task control.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 preserve-hours line is compact but abstracts the offered concession; A3 stock command adds clutter.
